Laurent

messages.author: 4a919e2a7108f363
messages.subject: Re: Bioc-teaching meeting: Monday 9 November at 2pm CET
parts:
Hi everyone,

just a reminder that the next Bioconductor teaching call will take place on Monday, November 9 at 2pm CET. The plan for this time is to discuss what properties we would need from a data set that could ideally be used throughout the intro module, and how/where we can find such a data set. Thus, we’d encourage everyone to give some thought to the types of figures/analyses that we would like to include in the module (based on the high-level objectives that we worked on previously), and what we would need from the data in order to achieve this goal. 

The jitsi link is the usual one: https://meet.jit.si/BioconductorTeaching 

See you on Monday,
Charlotte & Laurent

messages.author: 4a919e2a7108f363
messages.subject: Bioc-teaching meeting: Monday 7 December at 2pm CET
parts:
Hi everyone,

just a quick reminder of the Bioc teaching call on Monday, December 7 at 2pm CET. The jitsi link, as usual, is https://meet.jit.si/BioconductorTeaching.
The agenda is available in the Google Doc - the main topic will be exercise design, which Toby will kindly guide us through.
Last time we converged towards using the data set proposed by Kevin (from https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-018-07329-0) for the intro module. Kevin has prepared a repository with information on how to pull down the data here: https://github.com/kevinrue/bioc-teaching-intro. Running dev/geo-download.sh followed by dev/make-se.R should generate the SummarizedExperiment object (I just tried and it worked fine).

See you on Monday,
Charlotte & Laurent

messages.subject: Bioc-teaching meeting: Monday 11 January at 2pm CET
parts:
Hi everyone,

Happy New Year! Just a quick reminder that the next bioc-teaching call will take place on Monday, January 11 at 2pm CET. The jitsi link is https://meet.jit.si/BioconductorTeaching. One of the agenda items this time will be to discuss how the group can participate in the newly launched Carpentries lesson development study groups (https://carpentries.org/blog/2020/12/lesson-development-study-groups/).
In addition, we wanted to draw your attention to the fact that the Carpentries is currently running a bonus module on online training for certified Carpentries instructors (see more at https://carpentries-incubator.github.io/instructor-training-bonus-modules/bonus_module_calendar/index.html).

See you on Monday,
Charlotte & Laurent
